audit_findings.title: Post-AMI financing cost is absent from both OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $925 million post-closing term loan and $173.305 million pre-closing cash; annual interest unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The post-closing interest expense should reduce equity-level OE, while cash used for the acquisition should be removed from the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: At January 3, 2026 and December 28, 2024, we had no borrowings outstanding under the 2022 Credit Agreement.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated date mismatch. The $2.3 million anchor and July 4 bridge contain no interest on the $925 million borrowed July 27, yet the valuation is dated September 5 and assumes debt cost is already captured in OE. The bridge also adds $173.305 million of pre-closing cash without establishing how much remained after funding the transaction. The borrowing is more than four times the modeled base equity value of $206 million, and even a small financing charge would dwarf the OE anchor.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the opening post-AMI balance sheet and acquisition sources-and-uses schedule; determine closing cash, debt balances, effective interest rates, fees and hedges; then rerun OE and the bridge on the post-closing basis.

audit_findings.title: The numerator, denominator, and balance-sheet bridge describe different corporate perimeters
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.3 million legacy OE, 153.333 million valuation shares, $173.305 million July 4 cash and $0 July 4 debt, versus $925 million post-closing debt and approximately 5.2 million shares and RSUs issued as acquisition consideration
audit_findings.mechanism: Legacy-only OE supplies the numerator, post-closing securities affect the per-share denominator, and pre-closing cash and debt supply the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our fiscal 2025 was a 53 -week year that ended on January 3, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, although its net direction cannot be determined because AMI earnings are omitted while acquisition liabilities, financing costs and possibly consumed cash are also omitted. These components are large relative to the modeled $196 million to $211 million equity values, so alignment could materially alter or invalidate the valuation output.
audit_findings.action: Use AMI pro-forma financial statements or the first complete post-closing filing to calculate combined-company OE, post-closing cash and liabilities, and a reconciled post-closing diluted share count as of one common date; rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Recurring software and IP license investment may be missing from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Cash payments of $19.781 million in fiscal 2025, $16.708 million in fiscal 2024, $13.152 million in fiscal 2023 and $23.990 million in the first half of fiscal 2026; the fiscal-2025 amount is 8.6 times the $2.3 million anchor; maintenance portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If license amortization is added back to earnings without deducting the associated recurring investing cash outflow, OE is overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: Investing cash flows consist primarily of transactions related to capital expenditures and payments for software and intellectual property licenses .
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring cash payments and their scale are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not establish whether the OE bridge deducted them or how much represents maintenance rather than growth investment. Because even a modest maintenance fraction could exceed the $2.3 million anchor, the possible error is reasonably capable of changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year to the cash-flow statement and intangible-asset note; identify license-amortization add-backs and deduct maintenance or replacement license payments, with documented support for any growth-only exclusion; rerun the anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The share count may be neither free of duplication nor a true ceiling
audit_findings.magnitude: 153.333 million valuation shares versus 142.030272 million July 30 outstanding shares, a difference of 11.302728 million or 7.4% of the assumed denominator; removing the entire difference would raise base value only from approximately $1.34 to $1.45 per share, still 98.7% below the $115.90 price
audit_findings.mechanism: Duplicated acquisition securities would overstate the denominator and understate value per share; omitted maximum award payouts would understate the denominator and overstate value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: The awards may vest at 250 % or 200 %, depending on the executive, if the 75th percentile of the market condition is achieved, with 100 % of the units vesting at the 55th percentile, zero vesting if relative TSR is below the 25th percentile, and vesting scaling for achievement between the 25th and 75th percentile.
audit_findings.explanation: Duplication and maximum-payout treatment remain unresolved, but the known denominator scale is not capable of bridging the valuation conclusion. Even the extreme favorable assumption that all 11.302728 million shares above the July 30 cover count were duplicative increases the computed base value by only about 8%, leaving it approximately $114.45 below the market price. Maximum award dilution would move value in the opposite direction.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the 153.333 million count to transfer-agent records, acquisition consideration and replacement awards, remove overlap, and apply contractual payout maxima; update per-share outputs, but no conclusion-changing rerun is indicated from the demonstrated scale alone.

audit_findings.title: Repeated restructuring costs must not be normalized away as isolated one-offs
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.908 million in fiscal 2023, $12.291 million in fiscal 2024, $4.044 million in fiscal 2025 and $0.625 million in the first half of fiscal 2026; the fiscal-2025 amount is 1.8 times the $2.3 million anchor and the first-half 2026 amount is 27% of it
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding recurring restructuring charges back as one-offs raises normalized OE and the resulting operating present value.
audit_findings.evidence: Restructuring and other activity is generally comprised of expenses resulting from workforce reductions, cancellation of contracts, and consolidation of our facilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The repeated charges are demonstrated, but an actual valuation error is not established because the supplied OE bridge does not show whether they were added back. Their recurrence across every presented year undermines blanket one-off treatment, and their scale relative to the anchor makes any improper normalization potentially material.
audit_findings.action: Inspect every annual and interim OE bridge for restructuring add-backs; retain workforce, facility and contract-rationalization costs unless transaction-specific evidence establishes nonrecurrence; then recompute the OE series, anchor and scenarios.
